questions.prompt: What does the 'R' in a tire size such as 225/65R17 mean?
questions.explanation: The R stands for radial construction, where the ply cords run radially across the tire.

questions.prompt: In the size 225/65R17, what does 65 represent?
questions.explanation: 65 is the aspect ratio: sidewall height is 65 percent of the section width.

options.label: B
options.body: The aspect ratio - sidewall height as 65% of width

questions.prompt: A tire's DOT date code ends in '24' for its last two digits. What does that indicate?
questions.explanation: The last two digits of the DOT code are the year of manufacture.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the tread pattern's circumferential grooves?
questions.explanation: Circumferential grooves evacuate water from the contact patch to maintain grip in the wet.

options.label: B
options.body: To make the tire quieter only

options.label: D
options.body: To channel water away and resist hydroplaning

questions.prompt: What does a rim's offset describe?
questions.explanation: Offset is the distance from the hub mounting surface to the rim's centreline.

options.label: A
options.body: The distance between the mounting surface and the rim centreline

options.label: B
options.body: The diameter of the centre bore only

options.label: D
options.body: The width of the tire bead

questions.prompt: Tread wear bars level with the tread surface indicate the tire is:
questions.explanation: Wear bars flush with the tread mean the tread is worn to its minimum usable depth.

options.label: B
options.body: At or near the legal minimum tread depth and due for replacement

questions.prompt: How does a self-supporting run flat tire keep working after a puncture?
questions.explanation: Run flat sidewalls are reinforced so they can carry the load for a limited distance at reduced speed with zero pressure.

options.label: A
options.body: It seals itself with liquid inside

options.label: B
options.body: Its reinforced, stiff sidewalls support the vehicle load with no air pressure

options.label: C
options.body: It has a solid rubber core

options.label: D
options.body: The rim locks the bead so air cannot escape

questions.prompt: After driving on a deflated run flat tire, best practice is generally to:
questions.explanation: Run flats driven deflated can suffer hidden structural damage, so replacement is the safe best practice.

options.label: A
options.body: Repair it like any standard tire in all cases

options.label: B
options.body: Drive indefinitely if it still holds shape

options.label: C
options.body: Replace it, because internal sidewall damage may not be visible

questions.prompt: A direct TPMS system measures pressure using:
questions.explanation: Direct TPMS uses a pressure sensor inside each wheel that transmits actual pressure.

options.label: B
options.body: Sensors mounted inside each wheel/tire assembly

questions.prompt: After rotating tires on a vehicle with direct TPMS, what may be required?
questions.explanation: A relearn matches each sensor ID to its new wheel position so the display shows the correct corner.

options.label: B
options.body: A relearn procedure so the system knows each sensor's new position

courses.title: Best Practice Tire Fitment
moduleTitles: Best Practice Standard Tire Strip and Fitment
Best Practice Low Profile / Run Flat Tire Strip and Fit

questions.prompt: Static imbalance in a wheel assembly will most likely cause:
questions.explanation: Static imbalance makes the heavy spot lift and drop each revolution, causing a hop.

options.label: B
options.body: A vertical hop or bounce as speed increases

options.label: C
options.body: A constant pull to one side

questions.prompt: Before balancing a wheel, best practice is to:
questions.explanation: Old weights and dirt change the result, so the assembly is cleaned and old weights removed first.

options.label: A
options.body: Add extra weights to compensate for dirt

options.label: B
options.body: Remove old weights and clean the rim and tire

options.label: D
options.body: Spin it with the valve cap removed only

questions.prompt: A balancer asks for weights in two planes. This corrects:
questions.explanation: Two-plane balancing corrects dynamic imbalance, which produces a wobbling couple force.

questions.prompt: When stripping a tire from a rim, the bead must first be:
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Standard Tire Strip and Fitment
questions.explanation: Both beads must be broken free from their seats before the tire can be levered off safely.

options.label: C
options.body: Pushed off the bead seat (broken) on both sides

questions.prompt: Why is lubricant applied to tire beads during fitment?
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Standard Tire Strip and Fitment
questions.explanation: Bead lubricant reduces friction so the bead passes over the rim flange and seats evenly.

options.label: A
options.body: To glue the bead to the rim

options.label: B
options.body: To help the bead slide over the rim and seat without damage

options.label: D
options.body: To stop the tire rotating on the rim permanently

questions.prompt: When seating beads during inflation, the technician should:
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Standard Tire Strip and Fitment
questions.explanation: Bead seating is done with restraint/clip-on chuck and never above the maker's maximum seating pressure.

options.label: A
options.body: Stand directly over the tire with no restraint

options.label: B
options.body: Exceed maximum pressure until the beads pop, whatever it takes

options.label: C
options.body: Use a safety cage or clip-on chuck and stay within the stated maximum seating pressure

questions.prompt: The yellow dot on many new tires marks:
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Standard Tire Strip and Fitment
questions.explanation: The yellow dot marks the lightest point and is commonly aligned with the valve stem.

options.label: B
options.body: The lightest point, often aligned with the valve stem

questions.prompt: Low profile and run flat tires are harder to strip and fit mainly because:
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Low Profile / Run Flat Tire Strip and Fit
questions.explanation: Short, stiff sidewalls resist the flexing needed to clear the rim flange, so technique and machine helpers matter.

options.label: B
options.body: Their stiff, short sidewalls flex far less over the rim

options.label: C
options.body: They use a different valve type only

questions.prompt: When fitting a run flat tire, the TPMS sensor is at risk during:
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Low Profile / Run Flat Tire Strip and Fit
questions.explanation: Levers and the bead passing the sensor area can crack the sensor if its position is ignored.

options.label: B
options.body: Bead breaking and lever work near the valve/sensor position

options.label: C
options.body: Final torque of the wheel nuts

questions.prompt: Using press/roller helper arms on the changer for a stiff low profile tire helps to:
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Low Profile / Run Flat Tire Strip and Fit
questions.explanation: Helpers hold the bead in the drop centre, giving the slack needed to fit a stiff tire safely.

options.label: B
options.body: Keep the bead in the drop centre so it can pass over the flange without overstretching

questions.prompt: Sprung mass refers to:
questions.explanation: Sprung mass is everything the springs carry; wheels and brakes below the springs are unsprung mass.

options.label: B
options.body: The mass supported by the springs, such as body and engine

options.label: C
options.body: The mass below the springs only

questions.prompt: Reducing unsprung mass generally helps the tire to:
questions.explanation: Lighter unsprung parts follow road bumps more easily, keeping the tire planted.

options.label: B
options.body: Stay in contact with the road over bumps

questions.prompt: A coil spring's rate describes:
questions.explanation: Spring rate is force per unit of deflection, for example newtons per millimetre.

options.label: B
options.body: How much force is needed to compress it a given distance

questions.prompt: A broken or sagging spring will most directly affect:
questions.explanation: A weak spring lowers ride height, which changes camber and other alignment angles.

options.label: A
options.body: Ride height and wheel alignment angles

questions.prompt: The shock absorber's job is to:
questions.explanation: Shocks damp spring movement by converting motion into heat in the oil; springs carry the load.

options.label: C
options.body: Control (damp) spring oscillation after a bump

questions.prompt: A worn shock absorber will most likely cause:
questions.explanation: Weak damping lets the wheel keep bouncing, which cups the tread and hurts control.

options.label: B
options.body: Continued bouncing after a bump and uneven (cupped) tire wear

questions.prompt: Excess play in a suspension ball joint is best checked by:
questions.explanation: Ball joint wear is measured as movement under the maker's specified load condition.

options.label: B
options.body: Loading/unloading the joint as directed and measuring movement against specification

options.label: D
options.body: Turning the steering to full lock only

questions.prompt: Control arms locate the wheel by:
questions.explanation: Arms and links position the hub and define how it moves through suspension travel.

options.label: B
options.body: Connecting the knuckle/hub to the body or subframe and controlling its movement path

questions.prompt: An anti-roll (stabilizer) bar reduces body roll by:
questions.explanation: The bar resists one side compressing more than the other, which is what body roll is.

options.label: B
options.body: Twisting to transfer load between the two sides when they move differently

questions.prompt: Worn suspension bushes commonly cause:
questions.explanation: Perished or split bushes allow excess movement, causing noise, play and alignment shift under load.

options.label: B
options.body: Clunks over bumps, vague handling and uneven tire wear

courses.title: Understanding Suspension Systems
moduleTitles: MACPERSON Strut System Components and Operation
Torsion Bar System Components and Operations
Double Wishbone System Components and Operations

questions.prompt: In a MacPherson strut system, the strut itself:
questions.moduleTitle: MACPERSON Strut System Components and Operation
questions.explanation: The strut is a structural member: it locates the wheel, carries the spring, and steers with the knuckle.

options.label: A
options.body: Is only a shock absorber and carries no load path

options.label: B
options.body: Forms part of the steering/suspension location, with the spring around it and a top mount to the body

questions.prompt: The strut top mount bearing allows:
questions.moduleTitle: MACPERSON Strut System Components and Operation
questions.explanation: The top bearing lets the whole strut assembly pivot smoothly during steering.

options.label: B
options.body: The strut to rotate as the steering turns

questions.prompt: Before removing a strut spring, the spring must be:
questions.explanation: A loaded coil spring stores dangerous energy and must be compressed with the correct tool first.

options.label: C
options.body: Safely compressed with a proper spring compressor

options.label: D
options.body: Left fully loaded while bolts are removed

questions.prompt: Oil misting/leaking from a strut body and a failed bounce test indicate:
questions.explanation: Leakage plus poor damping means the strut is worn; struts are normally renewed in pairs.

options.label: B
options.body: A worn strut needing replacement, normally in axle pairs

questions.prompt: A torsion bar spring works by:
questions.moduleTitle: Torsion Bar System Components and Operations
questions.explanation: The bar twists to provide spring force, anchored at one end and driven by the arm at the other.

options.label: B
options.body: Twisting along its length as the control arm moves

questions.prompt: Ride height on a torsion bar system is commonly adjusted by:
questions.moduleTitle: Torsion Bar System Components and Operations
questions.explanation: The adjuster changes the bar's preload angle, raising or lowering ride height.

options.label: B
options.body: Turning the anchor adjuster bolt to add or reduce bar preload (twist)

questions.prompt: During torsion bar inspection, cracking or heavy corrosion on the bar is serious because:
questions.explanation: The bar works under high torsional stress, so cracks can lead to sudden failure.

options.label: B
options.body: A fatigued bar can snap suddenly under its torsional load

questions.prompt: A double wishbone system uses:
questions.moduleTitle: Double Wishbone System Components and Operations
questions.explanation: Two arms of different effective length control how camber changes as the wheel rises and falls.

options.label: B
options.body: Upper and lower arms, which control camber change through travel

questions.prompt: Play found at the wheel on a double wishbone system could come from:
questions.explanation: Several joints can produce play, so each is checked separately under the right load.

options.label: A
options.body: Ball joints, arm bushes or the wheel bearing - each must be isolated to find the source

questions.prompt: An electronic kinetic dynamic suspension system improves both roll control and off-road articulation by:
questions.explanation: It varies anti-roll bar resistance: stiff against roll on road, relaxed for wheel articulation off road.

options.label: B
options.body: Hydraulically/electronically controlling the anti-roll bars so they can stiffen on road and free up off road

questions.prompt: In an air suspension system, the steel coil spring is replaced by:
questions.explanation: Air springs use pressurised air in a rubber bellows to support the load.

options.label: B
options.body: A flexible air spring (air bag) filled with compressed air

questions.prompt: Ride height in an air suspension system is monitored by:
questions.explanation: Height sensors report body position and the module commands the compressor or exhaust valve to correct it.

options.label: A
options.body: Height sensors linked to the control module, which adds or vents air to correct height

questions.prompt: The air compressor in this system primarily:
questions.explanation: The compressor provides the air needed to inflate the springs and restore ride height.

options.label: B
options.body: Supplies pressurised air to fill the springs/reservoir when height must rise

questions.prompt: A vehicle that sags at one corner overnight most likely has:
questions.explanation: A slow overnight drop at one corner points to an air leak in that corner's circuit.

options.label: B
options.body: An air leak at that corner's spring, line or valve

questions.prompt: Before jacking or lifting an air suspension vehicle, best practice is to:
questions.explanation: Service/jack mode stops the system levelling while lifted, which could move the vehicle or damage parts.

options.label: B
options.body: Follow the maker's procedure - often selecting jack/service mode or disabling the system

options.label: D
options.body: Remove the battery from the car and discard it

questions.prompt: A dryer unit is fitted in many air suspension systems to:
questions.explanation: Removing moisture prevents corrosion and freezing inside valves and air lines.

options.label: B
options.body: Remove moisture from the compressed air to protect valves and springs

questions.prompt: An active/adaptive shock absorber changes its damping by:
questions.explanation: Adaptive dampers vary their valving electrically so damping can change in milliseconds.

options.label: B
options.body: Varying oil flow through an electrically controlled valve (or changing fluid properties) in response to module commands

questions.prompt: Inputs an active suspension module commonly uses include:
questions.explanation: The module blends sensor inputs and the selected mode to set damping for each corner.

options.label: B
options.body: Steering angle, wheel/body movement, vehicle speed and drive mode

questions.prompt: In a firmer sport drive mode, active shocks will generally:
questions.explanation: Sport mode firms damping to control body movement more tightly.

options.label: B
options.body: Increase damping to limit body roll, pitch and dive

questions.prompt: A failed active shock electrical connector will most likely:
questions.explanation: With no control signal the damper defaults to a preset rate and the system logs a fault.

options.label: B
options.body: Set a fault code and cause that damper to default to a fixed (failsafe) damping setting

questions.prompt: In a manual rack and pinion, turning the steering wheel moves the rack by:
questions.explanation: The pinion rotates against the rack teeth, sliding the rack side to side to steer the wheels.

options.label: B
options.body: The pinion gear meshing with teeth on the rack, converting rotation into linear movement

questions.prompt: Steering ratio describes:
questions.explanation: Ratio compares steering wheel input to road wheel output; higher ratios need more turns.

options.label: B
options.body: How many degrees the steering wheel turns for a given degree of road wheel movement

options.label: C
options.body: The size of the steering wheel

questions.prompt: In hydraulic power steering, assistance comes from:
questions.explanation: The pump supplies pressurised fluid that helps move the rack when the wheel is turned.

options.label: B
options.body: Pressurised fluid from an engine-driven pump acting in the rack or box

options.label: C
options.body: An electric motor on the column

questions.prompt: Heavy steering with whining noise from the pump most often indicates:
questions.explanation: Low or aerated fluid starves the pump, causing noise and loss of assistance.

options.label: B
options.body: Low fluid level or air in the system (aeration)

questions.prompt: A rotary control valve in the steering gear works to:
questions.explanation: The valve senses torsion bar twist from driver effort and ports fluid to assist in that direction.

options.label: A
options.body: Direct pressurised fluid to the correct side of the piston in proportion to steering effort

questions.prompt: Electro hydraulic power steering differs from conventional hydraulic steering because:
questions.explanation: An electric motor drives the hydraulic pump, so assistance can be provided without the engine driving a belt pump.

options.label: B
options.body: Its pump is driven by an electric motor rather than directly by the engine

questions.prompt: One advantage of electro hydraulic steering is that the module can:
questions.explanation: Demand-based pump speed cuts parasitic load compared with a constantly driven pump.

options.label: A
options.body: Vary pump speed with demand - running slower when no assistance is needed, saving energy

questions.prompt: In electric power steering (EPS), assistance is provided by:
questions.explanation: EPS uses a motor, controlled by a module using torque sensor input, to add steering assistance.

options.label: B
options.body: An electric motor acting on the column, pinion or rack

questions.prompt: The steering torque sensor in an EPS system measures:
questions.explanation: Torque sensor input tells the module how much assistance to apply and in which direction.

options.label: B
options.body: How hard and in which direction the driver is turning the wheel

questions.prompt: After replacing an EPS component or performing an alignment, a scan tool procedure often required is:
questions.explanation: The steering angle sensor must be recalibrated so EPS and stability systems know true straight-ahead.

options.label: B
options.body: Steering angle sensor calibration / zero point relearn

questions.prompt: Camber is defined as:
questions.explanation: Camber is the wheel's tilt from vertical viewed from the front; top out is positive.

options.label: A
options.body: The forward tilt of the steering axis

options.label: B
options.body: The inward or outward tilt of the top of the wheel when viewed from the front

options.label: C
options.body: The difference in angle between the two front wheels in a turn

options.label: D
options.body: The direction the rear wheels point

questions.prompt: Excessive negative camber will wear the tire mainly on its:
questions.explanation: Negative camber loads the inner shoulder, so that edge wears fastest.

questions.prompt: Caster mainly affects:
questions.explanation: Positive caster helps the wheels self-centre and improves stability.

questions.prompt: Toe is best described as:
questions.explanation: Toe compares the direction of the front and rear edges of a pair of tires from above.

options.label: A
options.body: The tilt of the wheel from the front

options.label: B
options.body: Whether the fronts of the tires point in toward each other, out, or straight ahead, viewed from above

questions.prompt: Excess toe-in or toe-out will most quickly cause:
questions.explanation: Incorrect toe scrubs the tread sideways as the vehicle travels, wearing it rapidly.

options.label: B
options.body: Feathered/scuffed tire tread wear and possible steering pull or wander

questions.prompt: Steering axis inclination (SAI) is:
questions.explanation: SAI is a built-in angle used diagnostically to spot bent parts when it differs side to side.

options.label: A
options.body: Adjustable on every car with shims

options.label: B
options.body: The inward tilt of the steering axis from vertical, viewed from the front, largely set by design

options.label: D
options.body: Measured only on the rear axle

questions.prompt: Included angle is the combination of:
questions.explanation: Included angle = SAI + camber, and helps identify bent struts, knuckles or arms.

questions.prompt: Thrust angle describes:
questions.explanation: Thrust angle is the rear toe direction relative to centreline; the vehicle tends to travel along it.

options.label: A
options.body: The angle of the steering wheel only

options.label: B
options.body: The direction the rear axle points compared with the vehicle centreline

options.label: C
options.body: The pitch of the body under braking

options.label: D
options.body: The angle of the front bumper

questions.prompt: Ackermann (toe-out on turns) allows:
questions.explanation: Ackermann geometry matches each front wheel to its different turning radius, reducing scrub.

options.label: A
options.body: Both front wheels to turn at exactly the same angle

options.label: B
options.body: The inside wheel to turn more sharply than the outside wheel, because it follows a smaller radius

questions.prompt: Before measuring any alignment angles, the technician should first check:
questions.explanation: Alignment readings are meaningless if ride height, pressures or worn parts are wrong, so these are checked first.

options.label: B
options.body: Ride height, tire pressures and sizes, and for worn or loose steering/suspension parts

options.label: C
options.body: Fuel level only and nothing else

courses.title: Braking System Essentials
moduleTitles: Drum Brake Systems Components and Operations
Drum Brake Systems Configuration and Maintenance

questions.prompt: Brakes slow the vehicle by converting kinetic energy into:
questions.explanation: Friction between pad/lining and disc/drum turns motion energy into heat.

questions.prompt: Hydraulic brake force works on Pascal's principle, which states:
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle is why pedal force at the master cylinder reaches every wheel.

options.label: A
options.body: Pressure in a confined fluid acts only downward

options.label: B
options.body: Pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions

options.label: C
options.body: Fluid pressure disappears in long lines

options.label: D
options.body: Air in the lines improves pressure

questions.prompt: Brake fluid must be hygroscopic-managed because it:
questions.explanation: Absorbed water drops the boiling point, risking vapour and a spongy pedal under hard braking.

options.label: B
options.body: Absorbs moisture over time, which lowers its boiling point and can corrode parts

options.label: C
options.body: Is the same as engine oil

questions.prompt: Mixing or using the wrong specification of brake fluid can cause:
questions.explanation: Fluids and seals are matched by specification; wrong fluid can damage rubber parts.

options.label: B
options.body: Seal swelling/damage and reduced performance - only the specified DOT grade should be used

questions.prompt: A tandem master cylinder has two separate hydraulic circuits so that:
questions.explanation: Splitting the system into two circuits provides a failsafe if one circuit leaks.

options.label: A
options.body: The brakes work twice as fast

options.label: B
options.body: If one circuit fails, the other can still provide braking on its wheels

questions.prompt: The compensating (bypass) port in the master cylinder allows:
questions.explanation: The port keeps the circuit filled and fully released when the pedal is up.

options.label: B
options.body: Fluid to return to the reservoir and release pressure when the pedal is released, and make up for pad wear

questions.prompt: In a disc brake, braking force is produced when:
questions.explanation: Hydraulic pressure drives the caliper piston(s) to clamp the pads onto the disc.

options.label: B
options.body: The caliper squeezes pads against both faces of a rotating disc

questions.prompt: A floating caliper moves on its slides so that:
questions.explanation: As the piston pushes the inner pad in, the sliding caliper pulls the outer pad into the disc.

options.label: A
options.body: Only the inner pad ever touches the disc

options.label: B
options.body: Both pads apply evenly - piston pushes one pad and the caliper reaction pulls the other in

options.label: D
options.body: The wheel can be removed without tools

questions.prompt: In a drum brake, the shoes are forced outward against the drum by:
questions.moduleTitle: Drum Brake Systems Components and Operations
questions.explanation: Hydraulic pressure in the wheel cylinder pushes its pistons and the shoes into the drum.

questions.prompt: Self-adjusters on drum brakes maintain:
questions.moduleTitle: Drum Brake Systems Configuration and Maintenance
questions.explanation: The adjuster takes up lining wear so pedal travel and parking brake action stay correct.

options.label: B
options.body: Correct shoe-to-drum clearance as the linings wear

courses.title: Advanced Braking System
moduleTitles: Hydraulic Pressure Control and Safety Valves

questions.prompt: A proportioning valve in the brake system:
questions.moduleTitle: Hydraulic Pressure Control and Safety Valves
questions.explanation: As weight transfers forward, the rears need less pressure; the valve reduces it to avoid lockup.

options.label: B
options.body: Limits/reduces hydraulic pressure to the rear brakes under hard braking to help prevent rear lockup

questions.prompt: A metering (hold-off) valve on some front disc / rear drum systems:
questions.moduleTitle: Hydraulic Pressure Control and Safety Valves
questions.explanation: Metering holds off the front discs briefly so front and rear brakes apply together.

options.label: B
options.body: Delays pressure to the front disc brakes slightly until the rear drums overcome return spring pressure

questions.prompt: The pressure differential (warning) valve's main job is to:
questions.moduleTitle: Hydraulic Pressure Control and Safety Valves
questions.explanation: A piston shifts when one circuit loses pressure and operates the warning lamp switch.

options.label: B
options.body: Detect a pressure loss difference between the two circuits and turn on the brake warning lamp

questions.prompt: A combination valve packages together functions such as:
questions.moduleTitle: Hydraulic Pressure Control and Safety Valves
questions.explanation: Many vehicles combine those three valve functions in a single combination valve.

options.label: B
options.body: Metering, proportioning and pressure differential warning in one body

questions.prompt: If a proportioning valve sticks and sends full pressure to the rear brakes, the likely symptom is:
questions.moduleTitle: Hydraulic Pressure Control and Safety Valves
questions.explanation: Excess rear pressure lets the lightly loaded rear wheels lock and skid first.

options.label: A
options.body: Rear wheels lock early under firm braking

questions.prompt: In a vacuum-suspended booster, at rest both sides of the diaphragm are:
questions.explanation: Vacuum-suspended means vacuum acts on both sides at rest; applying the pedal admits air to one side to create assist.

options.label: B
options.body: Under vacuum, suspended - pressure difference is only created when braking

questions.prompt: When the pedal is applied in a vacuum booster, assistance is produced because:
questions.explanation: The pressure difference across the diaphragm provides the extra push on the master cylinder.

options.label: B
options.body: Atmospheric pressure admitted to the rear chamber pushes the diaphragm against the vacuum in the front chamber

questions.prompt: A failed booster vacuum check valve or hose will most likely cause:
questions.explanation: Without stored vacuum the booster cannot assist, so pedal effort rises sharply.

options.label: B
options.body: A hard pedal with little or no assistance, especially after the engine stops or on repeated applications

questions.prompt: A hissing sound at the pedal inside the cabin when braking can indicate:
questions.explanation: Hissing with poor assist points to a booster air leak or diaphragm fault.

options.label: B
options.body: Air leaking into the booster past a torn diaphragm or faulty air valve

questions.prompt: A booster with a ruptured diaphragm will typically show:
questions.explanation: The leak loses assist and upsets engine vacuum, so idle can suffer too.

options.label: B
options.body: Hard pedal, poor assist and possibly rough idle from the vacuum leak

courses.title: ABS Operations and Testing
moduleTitles: Wheel Speed Sensor Operation and Testing

questions.prompt: The main purpose of ABS is to:
questions.explanation: By modulating pressure to a wheel about to lock, ABS preserves steering ability.

options.label: A
options.body: Shorten every stop on every surface

options.label: B
options.body: Prevent wheel lockup during braking so the driver keeps steering control

questions.prompt: During an ABS event the hydraulic modulator can, for each controlled wheel:
questions.explanation: ABS cycles pressure - hold, release, reapply - many times per second to keep the wheel near peak grip.

options.label: B
options.body: Hold, release (dump) and reapply pressure in rapid cycles

options.label: C
options.body: Drain all fluid to the reservoir

questions.prompt: Pedal pulsation and noise during a hard ABS stop on a slippery surface are:
questions.explanation: Pulsation is expected during ABS operation; the driver should keep firm pedal pressure.

options.label: B
options.body: Normal signs that the modulator and pump are working

options.label: D
options.body: A reason to release the pedal completely

questions.prompt: A passive (inductive) wheel speed sensor generates:
questions.moduleTitle: Wheel Speed Sensor Operation and Testing
questions.explanation: Passive sensors produce an AC signal that grows in frequency and voltage as speed increases.

options.label: B
options.body: An AC voltage signal whose frequency and amplitude rise with wheel speed, as teeth pass the sensor tip

options.label: C
options.body: A digital square wave of fixed amplitude

questions.prompt: An active wheel speed sensor differs because it:
questions.moduleTitle: Wheel Speed Sensor Operation and Testing
questions.explanation: Active sensors are supplied with power and can detect very low and even directional wheel speed.

options.label: B
options.body: Is powered by the module and produces a switching (digital-type) signal that can be read down to near zero speed

questions.prompt: Excessive air gap or a damaged tone ring on a passive sensor will most likely cause:
questions.moduleTitle: Wheel Speed Sensor Operation and Testing
questions.explanation: Too large a gap or missing teeth weakens/interrupts the signal, worst at low wheel speed.

options.label: B
options.body: A weak or dropout signal, especially at low speed, and a possible ABS fault

options.label: D
options.body: A firmer pedal at all times

questions.prompt: A wheel speed sensor circuit fault code with an open circuit would be confirmed by:
questions.explanation: Circuit testing - resistance, continuity and wiring checks - confirms an open before parts are replaced.

options.label: A
options.body: Guessing and replacing the module first

options.label: B
options.body: Measuring sensor circuit continuity/resistance and checking for opens or high resistance against specification

questions.prompt: A sensor signal that drops out only over bumps most suggests:
questions.explanation: Movement-related dropouts point to intermittent connections, found by wiggling the harness while watching live data or a scope.

options.label: A
options.body: A completely failed sensor element only

options.label: B
options.body: An intermittent wiring/connector fault that opens with movement - confirmed with a wiggle test while monitoring the signal

questions.prompt: The ABS pump motor's job during an ABS event is to:
questions.explanation: The pump restores the pressure that the release solenoids dumped so braking can be reapplied.

options.label: B
options.body: Return released brake fluid pressure to the circuit / build pressure for reapply

questions.prompt: If the pump motor does not run when commanded in a scan tool active test, the next checks should include:
questions.explanation: A no-run pump is diagnosed electrically: feed, ground, relay control and the motor itself.

options.label: B
options.body: Pump motor power feed, ground, relay and motor resistance/current against specification

courses.title: Park Brake Technology
moduleTitles: Cable Acuted Electric Park Brake Adjustment

questions.prompt: On a caliper type electric park brake, the parking brake is applied by:
questions.explanation: A motor and spindle mechanism in the caliper drives the piston to apply the pads mechanically.

options.label: A
options.body: A hand lever and long cable only

options.label: B
options.body: An electric motor on the caliper driving the piston out to clamp the pads

questions.prompt: Before servicing rear pads on a caliper type EPB, the technician must:
questions.explanation: Service mode winds the motor back safely; forcing it can damage the mechanism.

options.label: A
options.body: Force the piston back with a clamp straight away

options.label: B
options.body: Place the EPB in service/maintenance mode with a scan tool (or maker's procedure) to retract the motors

options.label: D
options.body: Remove the caliper from the car permanently

questions.prompt: After pad replacement on a caliper type EPB, the system typically needs:
questions.explanation: A calibration cycle sets the piston travel and confirms correct apply and release.

options.label: B
options.body: An apply/release or calibration cycle so the module relearns piston position and clamp force

options.label: D
options.body: New brake fluid in the booster

questions.prompt: An automatic apply feature on some EPB systems applies the park brake when:
questions.explanation: Auto-apply uses programmed conditions to set the brake without the driver pulling the switch.

options.label: B
options.body: Conditions such as engine off / door open / vehicle stopped are met, as programmed

questions.prompt: A cable actuated (cable puller) electric park brake works by:
questions.explanation: One motorised actuator tensions the existing cables to apply drum or caliper parking brakes.

options.label: B
options.body: An electric actuator unit that pulls the conventional parking brake cables

options.label: D
options.body: A vacuum servo pulling the hand lever

questions.prompt: A seized or stretched cable in a cable actuated EPB system will most likely cause:
questions.explanation: Cable condition decides how evenly actuator force reaches each wheel.

options.label: A
options.body: Equal braking on both sides always

options.label: B
options.body: Uneven application, weak holding on one side, or an actuator overload fault

questions.prompt: Holding ability of any park brake is finally tested by:
questions.explanation: The real test is whether the vehicle stays held on a slope on the park brake alone.

options.label: B
options.body: Confirming the vehicle holds securely on a gradient with the service brake released

questions.prompt: Cable actuated EPB adjustment matters because:
questions.moduleTitle: Cable Acuted Electric Park Brake Adjustment
questions.explanation: Too slack gives weak holding; too tight leaves the brakes dragging and overheating.

options.label: B
options.body: Correct cable free play/tension ensures full application without dragging when released

questions.prompt: A park brake that drags after adjustment - hot wheel and poor rolling - indicates:
questions.moduleTitle: Cable Acuted Electric Park Brake Adjustment
questions.explanation: Dragging means the brake is not fully releasing, commonly from over-tight or seized cables.

options.label: A
options.body: Adjustment too tight or a cable not fully releasing

questions.prompt: After adjusting a cable actuated EPB, best practice is to:
questions.moduleTitle: Cable Acuted Electric Park Brake Adjustment
questions.explanation: Cycling settles the cables, so adjustment and release are rechecked before the job is finished.

options.label: B
options.body: Cycle the brake several times, recheck adjustment and holding, and confirm both wheels release freely
